elements.element: Audit no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"
"upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company"

elements.element: Audit performed by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality
elements.evidence: "HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may ... have the right to inspect" — the auditing person is Vendor's own manager, with no confidentiality undertaking

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI." — cost sits wholly with Vendor, no shift-back trigger (more favourable to us)

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: clause grants a right to "inspect the records of the Company's General Manager" with no express exclusion of access to Company systems
"no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"
"no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice" exceeds the 15-day floor

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "fees incurred by HDI ... shall be borne by HDI"

offending_extra_words: may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect
reasons: The locked target was preferred, but the redline leaves two preferred elements unaddressed: the auditor is still Vendor's own General Manager rather than an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and there is no express bar on direct access to Customer systems.
The cost allocation is unconditionally on Vendor, which is at or better than both levels, so no change is needed there.

The result sits at the fallback (annual audit, ≥15 days' notice, Vendor-borne cost), so the clause is acceptable and would not normally be redlined; the shortfalls versus preferred are rationale points, not deviations.

Minimality fails on technique: the operation re-quotes and re-punctuates 19 words of untouched text ("may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect") to add a short frequency cap; a targeted insertion of "no more than once in any twelve (12) month period and" before "upon no less than thirty (30) days" achieves the same effect.
Intent is preserved: notice period, business-hours limit, scope of records and cost allocation remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
